shipped_originals.title_o: Association of Continuous Assessment of Step Count by Remote Monitoring With Disability Progression Among Adults With Multiple Sclerosis
shipped_originals.authors_o: Block; Bove; Zhao; Garcha; Graves; Romeo; Green; Allen; Hollenbach; Olgin; Marcus; Pletcher; Cree; Gelfand

blind_target.authors: Block VJ, Lizee A, Crabtree-Hartman E, Bevan C, Graves J, Bove R.
blind_target.title: Continuous daily assessment of multiple sclerosis disability using remote step count monitoring.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We obtained the original activity data from the CA ( 11 ,  12 ) and VA ( 13 ) cohorts, harmonized overlapping variables collected in both studies, and conducted secondary data analyses to replicate analyses in the CA cohort using the VA dataset ( 13 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Mirroring the approach used in the CA cohort ( 11 ,  12 ) study of 97 participants with MS using wrist-worn Fitbit activity monitors, we replicated key findings in the VA cohort ( 13 ) of 61 participants with MS with less severe disability, assessed using the hip-worn ActiGraph sensors.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Overall verdict explicitly states key findings of the CA studies (11, 12) were replicated in the independent VA cohort; smaller correlations and reliability are not framed as replication failure.

blind_target.evidence_quote: We investigated visual scanning behaviour in children with ASD during an EFT in an attempt replicating a previous study examining differences in visual search behaviour.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Abstract gives the present results but does not state the original result or identify its citation; comparison cannot be established.

shipped_originals.title_o: Developmental course of responsiveness to social reinforcement in normal children and institutionalized retarded children.

blind_target.title: The assessment of effectance motivation in normal and retarded children.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Based on descriptions available in the literature, we prepared tasks similar to those that were used to differentiate the performance of people with intellectual disability and controls in the original studies (Harter & Zigler, 1974; Yando & Zigler, 1971; Zigler & Balla, 1972).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results of our study do not support the hypothesis regarding differences between people with intellectual disability and people from the general population; as such, they are not in accordance with the results of previous studies conducted by Zigler and colleagues.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors state their overall results do not support the hypothesized group differences and disagree with the earlier studies; the statement covers the three named originals. Directional means and possible sample-size limitations do not override that verdict.
